test_name: 60-Second In-Field Alternaria vs Phytophthora Differentiation Key
university_source: UC Davis IPM & PAU Clinical Agronomy Key
in_field_steps: 1. Lesion Ring Test: Hold leaf toward sunlight. Observe necrotic spot. Concentric circular rings ('bullseye / target board') confirm Alternaria solani.
2. Abaxial Moisture Test: Check leaf underside early in morning. Absence of white downy mildew growth distinguishes Early Blight from Late Blight.
3. Stem Collar Check: Inspect stem base 2 cm above soil for dark brown sunken collar cankers.
rapid_diagnostic_outcome: If concentric rings present without white abaxial sporulation -> Confirmed Early Blight (Alternaria solani).

test_name: Rapid 60-Second Clear Water Tumbler Vascular Streaming Test
university_source: International Potato Center (CIP) & TNAU Diagnostic Key
in_field_steps: 1. Cut 3 cm of lower stem near ground level using clean blade.
2. Suspend cut stem in clear glass of clean water without touching bottom.
3. Observe for 60 seconds against dark background. Dense white milky bacterial streams oozing into clear water confirms Ralstonia solanacearum (Bacterial Wilt).
rapid_diagnostic_outcome: If milky streams flow within 60 seconds -> Confirmed Bacterial Wilt. If water stays completely clear -> Fusarium Fungal Wilt.

test_name: Diamond Spindle Lesion Field Identification Key
university_source: IRRI & ICAR National Rice Research Key
in_field_steps: 1. Inspect upper flag leaves. Look for diamond or spindle-shaped lesions with pointed ends.
2. Rub lesion center gently. Greyish ash-colored powdery center confirms Magnaporthe oryzae conidiophores.
3. Inspect neck node below panicle. Blackening indicates neck blast phase.
rapid_diagnostic_outcome: Diamond spindle lesions with ash-colored centers confirm Rice Blast.
